# Error and event codes

Every code the application can show a person is listed here with what it means and, for
errors and refusals, what to do next. Codes are stable identifiers: they are what the log,
the dashboard and an exported report all quote, so wording can change without breaking
anything that reads them.

| Code | Kind | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dashboard.diag_run` | event | a diagnostics run was started as a background job | — |
| `dashboard.export_saved` | event | a redacted export was written as text and JSON | — |
| `dashboard_bad_action` | error | an engine action was requested that is not one of on, off or toggle | use on, off or toggle |
| `dashboard_bad_level` | error | an unknown log level was requested | use one of debug, info, warn, error |
| `dashboard_bad_request` | error | the request body was not JSON this endpoint understands | reload the page; if you are calling the API yourself, send a JSON object in the documented shape |
| `dashboard_bad_token` | safety | the dashboard access token was wrong | the token belongs to a different run of the dashboard; restart the dashboard and use the address it prints |
| `dashboard_confirm_required` | safety | a change that writes to system settings was requested without explicit confirmation | preview first, then confirm; the dashboard never writes system settings from a request that did not ask for it knowingly |
| `dashboard_diag_unavailable` | error | the diagnostics engine is not available in this context | start the dashboard from the net-merge binary; the diagnostics need its process environment |
| `dashboard_encode_failed` | error | a response could not be encoded, so the dashboard refused to send a partial one | report this with the exported diagnostics; it has never been observed in testing |
| `dashboard_export_dir` | error | the export directory could not be created | check that the output directory is writable; the export is written nowhere else |
| `dashboard_export_write` | error | the export could not be written to disk | check free space and permissions on the output directory; nothing was uploaded anywhere |
| `dashboard_host_rejected` | safety | the request's Host header did not name the local machine, which is how the dashboard defends against DNS rebinding | use the 127.0.0.1 address the dashboard printed, not a hostname |
| `dashboard_job_not_done` | error | the result was asked for while the job was still running | poll the job until its status is done, then ask again |
| `dashboard_job_unknown` | error | a background job with that id does not exist in this run of the dashboard | job ids are per-run; start the work again from the page |
| `dashboard_logs_unavailable` | error | the event log could not be read | the in-memory event ring is not available in this context; start the dashboard from the net-merge binary |
| `dashboard_marker_failed` | error | the request to turn the engine on or off could not be written to the engine's marker file | check the free space and permissions of the state directory, then try again; the engine is untouched until the marker lands |
| `dashboard_remote_rejected` | safety | the request did not arrive over loopback, and the dashboard only ever serves the local machine | open the dashboard on the machine it runs on; it is not reachable from other devices by design |
| `dashboard_settings_invalid` | error | the settings that were submitted failed validation | the message names each problem; fix them in the Settings section and save again |
| `dashboard_settings_save_failed` | error | the settings file could not be written | check that the settings directory is writable and has free space; the previous file is left untouched when a save fails |
| `dashboard_settings_saved` | event | the settings file was written | — |
| `dashboard_state_dir` | error | the engine's state directory could not be prepared or read | check that the user account can write to the state directory reported in Diagnostics; on Windows it lives under the local application data folder |
| `dashboard_ttl_config_invalid` | error | the TTL configuration failed validation before anything was written | the details list each invalid field: the IPv4 TTL and IPv6 hop limit are 1..255, and the policy is one of none, list, all-except |
| `dashboard_ttl_config_save_failed` | error | the TTL configuration file could not be written | check the state directory's permissions and free space; no system setting was touched |
| `dashboard_ttl_history_failed` | error | the change history could not be read | the history file may be corrupt; it is only append-only, so the current values are unaffected. Inspect the state directory's ttl folder |
| `dashboard_ttl_inspect_failed` | error | the TTL/hop-limit settings could not be read | the details carry the platform's own error; read the Diagnostics section's TTL check for the same information with a full explanation |
| `dashboard_ttl_op_failed` | error | the TTL apply or restore did not complete | the details carry the manager's own outcome, which names each setting that failed and whether a rollback was complete |
| `dashboard_ttl_unavailable` | error | the TTL/hop-limit manager is not available in this context | the manager needs the platform backend; start the dashboard from the net-merge binary on Windows |
| `dashboard_unauthorized` | safety | the request carried no dashboard access token | open the address printed when the dashboard started; it contains the one-time token that starts a session |
| `dashboard_unauthorized_write` | safety | a state-changing request did not carry the token in its header | the page sends the header itself; a refusal here means the request did not come from the dashboard page |
| `diag_check_panic` | error | a check panicked and was contained, so it produced no result | the stack trace is in the log. One contained check never stops the others; report the exported diagnostics with this code |
| `diag_cmd_failed` | error | the command ran and reported failure | the evidence keeps the command, its exit code and its output; the check's summary says what that failure does and does not establish |
| `diag_cmd_unavailable` | error | the platform cannot run this command at all | the check reports what it would have established instead of pretending it ran |
| `diag_counters_unavailable` | error | the per-adapter byte counters could not be read | the platform may not expose them to this process; without counters the dashboard refuses to show a rate rather than showing zero |
| `diag_dns_error` | error | the resolver answered with an error | the name itself may not exist; the check distinguishes a resolvable-name problem from a resolver problem in its summary |
| `diag_dns_reserved_answer` | error | the resolver answered with an address reserved for documentation or internal use | this is usually a captive portal or a filtering resolver answering in place of the real record; open a browser or ask the network's operator |
| `diag_dns_server_unresponsive` | error | a configured DNS server did not answer a direct query | the machine may still resolve through another server; the check tests each configured server separately so the failing one is visible |
| `diag_dns_timeout` | error | the DNS lookup did not answer within its budget | try a second server; a single unresponsive resolver does not prove DNS is broken, and the check says which server it asked |
| `diag_dns_unconfigured` | error | no adapter reported a configured DNS server | resolution can still work through a system-wide or fallback configuration; the check states that it cannot establish otherwise |
| `diag_endpoint_invalid` | error | a configured test endpoint is not a usable host name or address | fix the endpoint in Settings > Diagnostics; the default is a well-known public name |
| `diag_endpoint_unresolved` | error | the check's own test endpoint could not be resolved | the endpoint's name is fixed and public; if it will not resolve, that is itself a DNS finding and the check reports it as one |
| `diag_engine_cli_unavailable` | error | the net-merge command line could not be run for this check | the check reports the path it tried. This usually means the binary was moved while running; restart the application |
| `diag_inventory_failed` | error | the adapter inventory could not be read for this check | the inventory error is carried in the evidence; run the adapter checks first, they usually name the cause |
| `diag_metric_unavailable` | error | the interface metric could not be read on this platform | the route table still shows the metrics; on platforms that do not expose the setting, the check says so instead of showing a zero |
| `diag_no_route` | error | no route to the destination exists | this is a routing problem, not a connectivity problem: the packet never left the machine. Compare the default routes in the Routing section |
| `diag_parse_failed` | error | a command produced output this build could not parse | this is a defect in the parser, not in the machine; the raw output is kept in the evidence so it can be reported. Other checks still ran |
| `diag_tcp_error` | error | the TCP connection attempt failed for a reason other than a timeout or a refusal | the evidence carries the socket error verbatim; it usually names the adapter or route involved |
| `diag_tcp_refused` | error | the destination answered and refused the connection | the path works: a reset or refusal is a reply. The port or service is the likely cause, not the network |
| `diag_tcp_timeout` | error | the TCP connection attempt got no answer before its deadline | a silent drop rather than a refusal. Firewalls and filtering middleboxes look exactly like this; the gateway and DNS checks say whether the path works at all |
| `diag_tool_missing` | error | a command the check needs is not installed or not on the search path | the evidence names the command. On Windows the networking checks use PowerShell's NetTCPIP cmdlets; make sure they are available, or run the check on a machine that has them |
| `diag_ttl_inspect_failed` | error | the TTL/hop-limit check could not read the settings | the TTL section reports the same failure with more detail; on a host with no supported mechanism this is expected and the check says so |
| `diag_ttl_read_partial` | error | some TTL/hop-limit settings were read and some were not | the check lists which ones; a partial read is reported as partial rather than as a clean result |
| `diag_udp_no_reply` | error | the UDP probe got no reply | UDP has no handshake, so silence proves very little. The check only claims a reply where the destination is one that answers by design, such as NTP |
| `diag_udp_unexpected_reply` | error | the UDP probe got a reply that did not match the request | a reply did arrive, which is what the check needed to establish; the mismatch is recorded rather than dropped |
| `engine_stale_adapter` | error | a route names an interface that no longer exists, usually left behind by a phone or adapter removed while the engine was running | run net-merge cleanup to remove the engine's own leftover routes; operating-system routes clear by themselves when the adapter returns or after a restart |
| `engine_start` | event | the engine was asked to start | — |
| `engine_uses` | event | the engine's own status file says which adapters it is using | — |
| `port_in_use` | error | the port the proxy needs is already taken by another process | the check names the holder when the platform allows it; close that program or configure a different port |
| `ttl_already_at_value` | error | the requested value is already in place | nothing to do; this is reported as a change that was not needed rather than as a failure |
| `ttl_busy` | safety | another change is in progress, or a previous run left its lock behind | wait for it to finish. A stale lock from a crashed process is reclaimed automatically; the details say whether that happened |
| `ttl_cancelled` | error | the operation was cancelled before it began or while it was in progress | nothing to do; re-run when you are ready |
| `ttl_captured` | event | the value in place was recorded before a change, so a restore can put it back exactly | — |
| `ttl_config_invalid` | error | the stored TTL configuration failed validation | open TTL > Configuration and fix the named fields; the defaults are shown meanwhile and no system setting was touched |
| `ttl_config_unreadable` | error | the stored TTL configuration could not be read and was quarantined rather than deleted | the previous file is kept beside the new one with a .corrupt- suffix; re-save the configuration from the TTL section |
| `ttl_error` | error | the TTL manager returned an error that has no more specific code | the message carries the platform's own text; include it in an exported report when asking for help |
| `ttl_no_captured_originals` | error | there is nothing to restore because no original values have been captured yet | capture happens automatically before the first change to a setting; this message means no change has been made yet |
| `ttl_permission_denied` | safety | the change needs administrator rights and this process does not have them | start the operation with elevation; the tray and the Control Center request it for that operation only. Nothing was changed |
| `ttl_read_failed` | safety | the value in place before the change could not be read, so the change was not attempted | without the original value there is no honest way to put it back. Fix the read failure first (the details name the setting) and try again |
| `ttl_rollback_incomplete` | error | a change failed and the automatic rollback could not put every value back | the outcome lists exactly which settings are still changed. Restore from the captured originals, or set the values by hand using the originals shown in TTL > Captured originals |
| `ttl_supported` | event | the platform probe found a mechanism for these settings | — |
| `ttl_timeout` | error | the operation did not finish inside its time budget | check the history for a partially applied change; a lock left by a crashed process is reclaimed automatically on the next attempt |
| `ttl_unsupported` | safety | this host has no supported mechanism for changing the packet-header value | nothing was changed. Per-interface TTL and hop limit are Windows settings; on other platforms the manager reports the values it cannot change instead of inventing a mechanism |
| `ttl_unsupported_platform` | safety | the TTL manager's write path only exists on Windows | inspection still works and reports the current values; changes are refused rather than attempted with an unsupported mechanism |
| `ttl_verify_failed` | error | the write ran but the value read back did not match, so it is reported as unconfirmed rather than as success | treat the setting as unknown; the history and the captured originals still allow a restore. This usually means something else on the system is managing the same value |
| `ttl_write_failed` | error | the platform rejected the write | the details carry the platform's own error. The original value is unchanged unless the detail says otherwise |
| `tun_driver_missing` | error | the virtual network driver the bonding engine needs is not present or not loadable | on Windows, run the repository's scripts/fetch-wintun.ps1 once to place the driver, then start the engine again; the driver is required only by the engine, not by the dashboard |

Registry size: 75 code(s).
